messages.subject: Problem with selecSETAR()
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I have problems implementing the function slectSETAR() to my database. I have 80 series of 80 countries from 1970 to 2008.   I do as follows:

for(i in 1:ncol(UNE)) {
print(i)
search <- selectSETAR(UNE[,i], m=2, thDelay=1)
print(mod.setar)
}

Next,

for(i in 1:ncol(UNE)) {
print(i)
set <- setar(UNE[,i], m=2, thDelay=1, th=mod.setar$th)
print(mod.setar)
}

Getting the following error messages:

[20] ERROR:
  With the threshold you gave, there is a regime with no observations!FALSE

When I change the "thDelay" argument from thDelay=1 to thDelay=2

[21] ERROR:
  thDelay too high

Someone could help me?

Thank you very much in adavance

messages.subject: possible bug in lstar
messages.body_plain:
Hi everybody,

just wanted to report a possible bug I encountered some time ago..

Doing this:

#--------------------------------------
require(tsDyn)
set.seed(1)

timeSeries <- c(33, 37, 41, 37, 37, 33, 77, 77, 85, 133, 57, 57, 49, 57, 53, 33, 49, 49, 73,
                 77, 61, 45, 53, 41, 65, 33, 53, 53, 41, 33, 73, 85, 77, 89, 101, 97, 57, 93,
                 57, 61, 69)#, 69, 73, 93, 57, 25, 41, 21, 5, 29)

lstarModel <- lstar(timeSeries, m=2, thDelay=1, trace=FALSE, control=list(maxit=1e5))
#--------------------------------------

results in:

Error in if (cost <= bestCost) { : missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed

As you see, some values at the end of the example data series is commented out, because it is normally used as test set. If all available data is used, the error does not occur.

Is the series too short? Am I using lstar not correctly?

Regards,
Christoph
